description: IP threat intelligence sources for iGaming fraud and proxy detection

sources.name: Tor Project Bulk Exit List
sources.format_notes: One IPv4 address per line, no comments
sources.notes: Official Tor Project exit node list. Most authoritative source for Tor exit IPs.

sources.name: FireHOL Tor Exits (TorDNSEL)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Mirrors TorProject TorDNSEL exit list. Aggregated into FireHOL format.

sources.name: FireHOL Tor Exits (1-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Tor exits seen in last 24 hours.

sources.name: FireHOL Tor Exits (7-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Tor exits seen in last 7 days. Broader coverage than current list.

sources.name: Emerging Threats Tor IPs
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Emerging Threats network Tor exit node list. Good secondary source.

sources.name: dan.me.uk Dynamic Tor Node List
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Dynamic list including non-exit Tor nodes. Broader than exit-only lists.

sources.name: SecOps-Institute Tor Exit Nodes
sources.format_notes: One IPv4 address per line
sources.notes: Community-maintained Tor exit node list. Good supplemental source.

sources.name: X4BNet VPN Provider IPs (IPv4)
sources.format_notes: One CIDR range per line (e.g., 2.56.16.0/22)
sources.notes: Curated list of IP ranges used by commercial VPN providers. Excellent for iGaming VPN detection.

sources.name: X4BNet VPN Provider IPs (IPv6)
sources.format_notes: One IPv6 CIDR range per line
sources.notes: IPv6 ranges for commercial VPN providers.

sources.name: X4BNet Datacenter IPs (IPv4)
sources.format_notes: One CIDR range per line
sources.notes: IP ranges belonging to datacenter and hosting providers. Key for detecting bot traffic and scripted players.

sources.name: mmpx12 HTTP Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT (e.g., 1.2.3.4:8080)
sources.notes: Actively updated open proxy list. Includes HTTP proxies.

sources.name: mmpx12 SOCKS4 Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: SOCKS4 proxies updated hourly.

sources.name: mmpx12 SOCKS5 Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: SOCKS5 proxies updated hourly.

sources.name: TheSpeedX HTTP Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: Large aggregated proxy list. High volume source.

sources.name: TheSpeedX SOCKS4 Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: SOCKS4 proxy list from TheSpeedX.

sources.name: TheSpeedX SOCKS5 Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: SOCKS5 proxy list from TheSpeedX.

sources.name: ShiftyTR Proxy List (Mixed)
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: Mixed HTTP/SOCKS proxy list.

sources.name: ShiftyTR SOCKS5 Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: SOCKS5 proxy list from ShiftyTR.

sources.name: hookzof SOCKS5 List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: Actively maintained SOCKS5 list.

sources.name: monosans HTTP Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: Frequently updated HTTP proxy list with good quality control.

sources.name: clarketm Raw Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: Curated proxy list with good reliability.

sources.name: roosterkid HTTPS Open Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Format: IP:PORT
sources.notes: HTTPS-specific proxy list.

sources.name: proxifly Free Proxy List (All)
sources.format_notes: Format: protocol://IP:PORT (e.g., socks5://1.2.3.4:1080)
sources.notes: Mixed protocol proxy list. URL format includes protocol prefix.

sources.name: stamparm IPsum Threat Intelligence
sources.format_notes: Tab-separated: IP<TAB>score. Lines with # are comments. Score = number of blocklists that flagged the IP.
sources.notes: Aggregates multiple threat intel feeds. Score >= 3 indicates high confidence malicious. Excellent for iGaming fraud detection.

sources.name: FireHOL Level 1 Blocklist
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments. Entries are CIDR ranges or single IPs.
sources.notes: Maximum protection with minimum false positives. Composed from DShield, Feodo, Spamhaus DROP/EDROP. Suitable for production blocking.

sources.name: FireHOL Level 2 Blocklist
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments. Entries are CIDR ranges or single IPs.
sources.notes: Broader abuse list with slightly higher false positive rate. Good for risk scoring.

sources.name: FireHOL Level 3 Blocklist
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments. Entries are CIDR ranges or single IPs.
sources.notes: Aggressive blocking. Higher false positives. Use for risk scoring, not hard blocking.

sources.name: FireHOL Abusers (1-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments. CIDR or single IPs.
sources.notes: Recent abusers from last 24 hours. Good for catching active attack sources.

sources.name: FireHOL Abusers (30-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments. CIDR or single IPs.
sources.notes: Persistent abusers over 30-day window. Broader list for risk scoring.

sources.name: FireHOL SOCKS Proxy List
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: SOCKS proxies aggregated into FireHOL format.

sources.name: FireHOL SOCKS Proxy (7-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: SOCKS proxies seen in last 7 days.

sources.name: FireHOL SOCKS Proxy (30-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: SOCKS proxies seen in last 30 days. Good for persistent proxy detection.

sources.name: FireHOL Botvrij Source IPs
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Malicious source IPs from botvrij.eu IOC feeds. Good for detecting bot registrations and scripted players.

sources.name: FireHOL Blocklist.de Bots
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: IPs reported for RFI attacks, IRC bots, registration bots, and comment spam bots.

sources.name: FireHOL BotScout (30-day)
sources.format_notes: Lines starting with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: IPs used by automated bots for forum registrations, spam, and form abuse. Directly relevant for iGaming account abuse.

sources.name: jhassine Server/Datacenter IP Addresses
sources.format_notes: CSV with header: cidr,hostmin,hostmax,vendor. Includes AWS, Azure, GCP, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, OVH, etc.
sources.notes: Named datacenter/cloud provider ranges with vendor attribution. Useful for distinguishing AWS from residential VPN traffic.

sources.name: stamparm Blackbook Malicious IPs
sources.format_notes: Tab-separated: IP<TAB>hostname. Lines with # are comments.
sources.notes: Actively malicious IPs with associated hostnames. Complements ipsum.

sources.name: abuse.ch Feodo Tracker C2 IPs
sources.format_notes: Lines with # are comments; remaining lines are IPv4 addresses
sources.notes: Botnet C2 IPs tracked by abuse.ch. Authoritative source for known malware infrastructure.

sources.name: DShield/SANS Recommended Block List
sources.format_notes: Tab-separated with header. Fields: Start IP, End IP, /24 CIDR, country, number of reports. Lines with # are comments.
sources.notes: Top 20 attacking /24 subnets. Authoritative threat intelligence from SANS ISC. Updated every 15 minutes.

sources.name: Spamhaus DROP List
sources.format_notes: CIDR followed by ; SBL reference. Lines with ; are comments.
sources.notes: Don't Route Or Peer list. Hijacked/unallocated IP space used for spam/malware. Very authoritative.

sources.name: Spamhaus eDROP List
sources.format_notes: CIDR followed by ; SBL reference. Lines with ; are comments.
sources.notes: Extended DROP list. Includes IP space controlled by criminals not in DROP. Essential complement to DROP.

tor.description: Tor network exit nodes and relay IPs
tor.notes: Players using Tor are bypassing geographic restrictions and obscuring identity. In most jurisdictions, iGaming operators must block Tor traffic.

vpn.notes: VPN usage may indicate geo-restriction bypass or identity concealment. Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction.

proxy.description: Open HTTP, SOCKS4, and SOCKS5 proxy servers
proxy.notes: Open proxies are commonly used for multi-accounting, bonus abuse, and geographic bypass.

datacenter.description: Cloud and datacenter provider IP ranges
datacenter.notes: Connections from datacenters may indicate bot activity, scripted players, or API abuse. However, legitimate users behind corporate VPNs may also appear here.

bot.description: Known bot and automated abuse IPs
bot.notes: Bot IPs are used for account creation abuse, credential stuffing, and automated gameplay.

abuse.description: Malicious IPs from multiple threat intelligence feeds
abuse.notes: IPs associated with malware, C2 infrastructure, spam, and active attacks.

output_files.tor-exits.txt: Deduplicated Tor exit node IPs (plain IPv4, one per line)
output_files.vpn-ips.txt: VPN provider CIDR ranges (one per line)
output_files.proxy-ips.txt: Open proxy IPs (plain IPv4, one per line, port stripped)
output_files.datacenter-ranges.txt: Datacenter/hosting provider CIDR ranges (one per line)
output_files.bot-ips.txt: Known bot and automated abuse IPs
output_files.abuse-ips.txt: Malicious/abusive IPs from threat intelligence feeds
output_files.consolidated-threats.txt: All categories merged, deduplicated, with category annotations
output_files.redis-load.sh: Redis SADD/SET commands for bulk import
output_files.cloudflare-kv-bulk.json: Cloudflare Workers KV bulk upload format
output_files.aws-waf-ipset.json: AWS WAF IP set JSON format
